study type: Secondary analysis of a prospective cohort study
exposure: Place of birth (freestanding midwifery unit vs. alongside midwifery unit)
outcome: Third or fourth degree perineal trauma
cohort: 27,938 low-risk women with singleton, term pregnancies
finding: Planned birth in a freestanding midwifery unit (FMU) was associated with a lower rate of instrumental delivery and a higher rate of straightforward vaginal birth compared to planned birth in an alongside midwifery unit (AMU), with no significant difference in adverse perinatal outcomes.
